attributes.allegiance: Roadwardens, provisionally. College of Levels, by seal — and by a house rule he has already broken, which neither body knows yet.
attributes.college: College of Levels, sealed. Sent across to Tallow Reach at sixteen as a pupil-leveller and kept there seven years; took the seal at twenty-three, then fourteen years of Warden service on top of it. The Wardenry may not lawfully set an instrument on the plain without a College-sealed hand, so his seal is the reason the centre survey exists at all — no other body would have been believed, and no Warden could have gone out alone.
attributes.origin: raised in Roadwarden service; no home rim-city he will name. The nearest thing to one is Tallow Reach, where he spent seven years at the College and where the roll he did not write on is kept. He calls it 'the far rim' and moves the conversation on.
attributes.tell: checks his own arithmetic in the margin of any paper to hand
attributes.two_masters: the Wardenry commissions him and pays him; the College sealed him and can lift the seal. One man, two bodies, one lead stamp — and the College's rule, the one that comes first, is that a finding goes on the roll before it goes to whoever paid for it. He has told neither body what he found.
attributes.unfiled: he should have entered a fair copy on the College roll before he stitched the packet shut. The entry is four lines and a rider — surveyor, ground, date, one line of result — out with the spring caravan and on the roll at the far rim by autumn. He drafted it twice, sent neither draft, and struck both seals over the thread instead. It is the only rule he has ever broken and he broke it by doing nothing, which is how he does most things.
attributes.voice: careful, qualified, retreats into figures when pressed; apologises in the middle of sentences and finishes them anyway
attributes.wants: the survey on the record without having to be the one who put it there

name: Denet Rasca
summary: Roadwarden surveyor, thirty-seven, and the author of the water survey -- he put the instruments down at the plain's centre himself and has been carrying the numbers, unpublished, ever since. He believes a measurement belongs on the record and cannot make himself say so out loud, because he has spent fourteen years licensing the crossings his own findings would end. He is travelling with Ysoly's caravan and has not told her why.
